claims.text: AWS grew 37% to $42.2B in the June 2026 quarter, and Anthropic and OpenAI have made multi-gigawatt Trainium commitments.
Amazon launched AWS in 2006 and built it into the largest public cloud.
AWS revenue rose 37% to $42.2B in the second quarter of 2026, its fastest growth in 18 quarters.
Both Amazon's AI business and its chips business passed $25B annual run rates.
Amazon said in April 2026 that Anthropic will secure up to 5 GW of current and future Trainium chips and that OpenAI committed to about 2 GW of Trainium capacity.
Amazon landed more than 2.1 million AI chips in the 12 months before its April 2026 report, more than half of them Trainium, and plans about $200B of capex in 2026.
Its trailing twelve-month free cash flow was negative $7.6B at the end of June 2026 as capex rose.
AWS revenue, Q2 2026 = $42.2B, up 37%
AI business run rate = Over $25B
Amazon 2026 capex plan = About $200B
Anthropic Trainium commitment = Up to 5 GW
OpenAI commitments = $38B (Nov 2025), about 2 GW of Trainium

claims.text: Cloud revenue grew 45% in the June 2026 quarter, and Alibaba raised HK$80B in August 2026 for AI infrastructure.
Alibaba's cloud revenue rose 45% to RMB 48.4B ($7.1B) in the quarter that ended June 2026, and AI-related product revenue reached RMB 12.4B ($1.8B).
Quarterly capex rose 75% to RMB 67.7B ($10.0B), which Alibaba attributes to procurement timing, added compute capacity and higher chip component prices.

In August 2026 Alibaba placed 710 million new shares for HK$80B (about $10.3B) and said it will spend the proceeds on AI infrastructure, including global computing capacity and hyperscale AI data centers.
T-Head's Zhenwu AI chips now serve more than 650 external customers through Alibaba Cloud.
Alibaba announced in February 2025 a plan to spend more than RMB 380B on cloud and AI infrastructure over three years.
Higher chip component prices already push up its capex.
